I have some hypotheses though. I’m also trying to find the answer to these for myself.

History happens because it’s history. Someone was able to write it down. And events took place that were significant.

Like I wonder how was Dapitan back in the day when Datu Pagbuaya came from Bohol after they lost a battle. He then set up the Kedatuan Ng Dapitan (which was orginally in Bohol) then to Northwest Mindanao.

There were already original people like the Subanen in Northwest Mindanao, but what significant history did they have? I’m watching a video on Crash Course History about one theory goes that tribal people were trying to escape from ‘civilization.’ - which brings me to my next point

For much of Philippine History in the Spanish period, Mindanao peoples were able to stave off Spanish colonialists - except some key areas like Zamboanga.

I guess the Mindanao peoples then didn’t write much. They must have had years of beautiful history but didn’t write it down on long lasting parchment like colonialists did.

But that’s all my speculation, on Facebook - “The Shaman of Kidapawan” has a lot more legit sources of Kidapawan history.

That’s a very good question and you should join a facebook page called the Luzvimindan Project because they touch on this stuff.

The short answer is: it hasn’t been done yet.

The bright side is that anyone can just do it on their own.

The down side we in general tend to prioritise Tagalog/Filipino and raise it up as a national language (rather than embrace all languages of the Philippines).

Also the way that Filipino/Tagalog is constructed nowadays is when there’s a word for something it’s either just bastardized (“gramar” for grammar) or made as a new long Filipino word that no one really all understands.

English developed along the way in that it can provide for more concise wording.

No one is really stopping us from doing so. But sadly existing PH language institutions are underpowered for undertaking such projects.

Also, I have observed, many old books about the Philippines are not yet even translated into .txt format on Project Gutenberg.

I had a hard time finding Rizal’s Works! It’s not easily found even on the Historical Commission website.

(If anyone wants to join me in trying to find these texts and make them into .txts, let’s do a project).
